course_title: Practical Exercise on European and Global Legal History
title: International law in the 20th century (Vec): from The Hague to the ICC

slides.title: Fin de siècle: the five forces out of which the war grew
slides.text: Vec's lecture opens with a set of five that describes the world around 1900 and at the same time explains why it ended in war. (1) EMPIRES AND STATES — empires with colonies stand alongside nation states, and international law must cope with both. (2) NATIONALISM. (3) MILITARISM. (4) MODERN TECHNOLOGY. (5) THE PUBLIC SPHERE — that is, the press and public opinion, an element easily forgotten: for the first time foreign policy is exposed to the pressure of newspaper readers, and that makes it less, not more, flexible. THE GUIDING QUESTION OF THE WHOLE LECTURE, worth knowing because it is a ready-made exam question: HOW DID INTERNATIONAL LAW IN THE LONG 20TH CENTURY TRANSFORM AND EXPAND ITS REGULATORY IDEAS AND AMBITIONS UNDER THE IMPRESSION OF DEMOCRATIZATION, AUTHORITARIANISM, THE COLD WAR, DECOLONIZATION AND GLOBALIZATION?

cards.q: Which five forces characterize the international law of the fin de siècle?
cards.a: EMPIRES AND STATES, NATIONALISM, MILITARISM, MODERN TECHNOLOGY and THE PUBLIC SPHERE. The last is easily forgotten: for the first time foreign policy is exposed to THE PRESSURE OF NEWSPAPER READERS, which makes it LESS, not more, flexible.

slides.title: The First World War as the first total war
slides.text: THE FIRST WORLD WAR (1914–1918) is called the first 'TOTAL WAR', and Vec adds to it the MASS KILLING OF THE ARMENIANS. NEW WEAPONS: THE MACHINE GUN, THE FLAMETHROWER, THE SUBMARINE, THE TANK, POISON GAS. Each of them posed a different problem for the law of war of the day — the submarine because it could not rescue survivors, gas because it was prohibited by the Hague Conventions, the tank because there were no rules for it at all. THERE WERE VIOLATIONS OF INTERNATIONAL LAW — and Vec adds what is most interesting for legal history: A DISCOURSE ABOUT INTERNATIONAL LAW AROSE, THAT IS, ACCUSATION AND JUSTIFICATION. The war did not lead to law ceasing to be taken seriously; on the contrary, IT WAS PRECISELY THEN THAT INTERNATIONAL LAW BECAME THE LANGUAGE IN WHICH THE BELLIGERENTS ACCUSED ONE ANOTHER AND JUSTIFIED THEMSELVES. That is proof that a norm operates even where it is broken.

cards.q: What was new about the First World War and what effect did it have on international law?
cards.a: It was the first 'TOTAL WAR', with the mass killing of the Armenians and new weapons (THE MACHINE GUN, FLAMETHROWER, SUBMARINE, TANK, POISON GAS). There were violations of law — but most interesting is that A DISCOURSE ABOUT INTERNATIONAL LAW AROSE, THAT IS, ACCUSATION AND JUSTIFICATION: it was precisely then that international law became THE LANGUAGE IN WHICH THE BELLIGERENTS ACCUSED ONE ANOTHER. A norm therefore operates even where it is broken.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

slides.title: The guilt clause and what it replaced
slides.text: This is the most valuable observation in the whole passage, and it is formulated in a single word in brackets. THE WAR GUILT CLAUSE TOOK THE PLACE OF 'MUTUAL OBLIVION'. Recall that since the Peace of Westphalia it had been a usual part of peace treaties to grant AN AMNESTY AND AN UNDERTAKING TO FORGET THE PAST — and that is exactly what Versailles abandoned. THE CONSEQUENCE IS CONCEPTUAL: WAR IS HENCEFORTH UNDERSTOOD AS AN UNLAWFUL ACT OF AGGRESSION, NOT SIMPLY AS A CLASH OF COMPETING INTERESTS. That is a fundamental break in all of international law: as long as war was a legitimate instrument of policy, guilt made no sense; once it is unlawful, there must be someone guilty. Other elements of the treaty follow from this: THE GERMAN EMPEROR WAS ARRAIGNED FOR OFFENCES, REPARATIONS were imposed and TERRITORIAL CESSIONS made. And Vec adds a one-word note on the reaction: PROTEST.

cards.q: What did the war guilt clause replace, and what is its conceptual consequence?
cards.a: It took the place of 'MUTUAL OBLIVION' — since the Peace of Westphalia it had been a usual part of peace treaties to grant AN AMNESTY AND AN UNDERTAKING TO FORGET. The consequence: WAR IS HENCEFORTH UNDERSTOOD AS AN UNLAWFUL ACT OF AGGRESSION, NOT AS A CLASH OF COMPETING INTERESTS. As long as war was a legitimate instrument of policy, guilt made no sense; once it is unlawful, THERE MUST BE SOMEONE GUILTY.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

slides.title: What the League of Nations actually built
slides.text: Besides the Covenant itself Vec names institutions and treaties that are often overlooked, and they are worth knowing, because they show that the interwar period was not merely a failure. THE PERMANENT COURT OF INTERNATIONAL JUSTICE (THE HAGUE, 1920) and the INTERNATIONAL LABOUR ORGANIZATION (ILO). THE DEMILITARIZED ZONE as an instrument for securing peace — and Vec also mentions the FRENCH OCCUPATION OF THE RUHR. FURTHER TREATIES AND DEVELOPMENTS: THE CONVENTION ON AIR NAVIGATION (1919) — an entirely new field, because law had not known the aeroplane; THE BRIAND-KELLOGG PACT (1928), by which states renounced war as an instrument of national policy; THE WORLD ECONOMIC CONFERENCE (1927); and TWO FURTHER GENEVA CONVENTIONS (1929), regulating the treatment of prisoners of war and of the wounded. The League's principal organs — THE ASSEMBLY, THE COUNCIL, THE SECRETARIAT — became THE MODEL FOR THE UN, and that is the best evidence that the institution proved itself as a form even though it failed as a power.

cards.q: Which institutions and treaties did interwar international law build?
cards.a: THE PERMANENT COURT OF INTERNATIONAL JUSTICE (The Hague, 1920) and the ILO; DEMILITARIZED ZONES; THE CONVENTION ON AIR NAVIGATION (1919) as an entirely new field; THE BRIAND-KELLOGG PACT (1928) renouncing war as an instrument of policy; THE WORLD ECONOMIC CONFERENCE (1927); TWO FURTHER GENEVA CONVENTIONS (1929). The League's organs (assembly, council, secretariat) became THE MODEL FOR THE UN.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

slides.title: Powerless law: the list on which the League failed
slides.text: Vec names the League's failure with a phrase to remember: 'POWERLESS LAW' — NO EFFECTIVE MEASURES WERE TAKEN AGAINST THE AGGRESSORS. And he gives a list worth knowing as a chain, because each link encouraged the next. (1) JAPAN INVADED MANCHURIA (1931). (2) ITALY ANNEXED ETHIOPIA (ABYSSINIA) IN 1935–36. (3) GERMANY LEFT THE DISARMAMENT CONFERENCE AND THE LEAGUE OF NATIONS (OCTOBER 1933). (4) IT SENT TROOPS INTO THE DEMILITARIZED RHINELAND (1936). (5) THE ANNEXATION OF AUSTRIA (1938). (6) THE SUDETENLAND (1938). (7) THE DESTRUCTION OF CZECHOSLOVAKIA (1939). Note the sequence: each step was larger than the last and each passed without sanction. That is what makes the list an argument — THE LEAGUE DID NOT FAIL BY ONE DECISION BUT BY A SERIES OF NON-DECISIONS.

cards.q: On what did the League of Nations fail? Name the chain.
cards.a: 'POWERLESS LAW' — NO EFFECTIVE MEASURES were taken against the aggressors: JAPAN IN MANCHURIA (1931), ITALY ANNEXES ETHIOPIA (1935–36), GERMANY LEAVES THE DISARMAMENT CONFERENCE AND THE LEAGUE (October 1933), TROOPS INTO THE DEMILITARIZED RHINELAND (1936), THE ANNEXATION OF AUSTRIA (1938), THE SUDETENLAND (1938), THE DESTRUCTION OF CZECHOSLOVAKIA (1939). Each step was larger and each passed without sanction — THE LEAGUE DID NOT FAIL BY ONE DECISION BUT BY A SERIES OF NON-DECISIONS.

slides.title: Five interwar theories of international law
slides.text: Vec divides interwar theory into FIVE CURRENTS, and the set of five is valuable, because usually only two are given. (1) THE VIENNA SCHOOL — KELSEN, KUNZ, VERDROSS; the pure theory of law and a monist conception of the relation between domestic and international law. (2) NATURAL-LAW APPROACHES. (3) THE POSITIVISTS. (4) SOVIET INTERNATIONAL LAW. (5) FASCIST INTERNATIONAL LAW. The last point deserves elaboration, because it rarely appears in textbooks and yet shows that even a dictatorship needs a legal theory. THE FEATURES OF FASCIST INTERNATIONAL LAW: (a) THE FIGHT AGAINST VERSAILLES, which in Germany was a CONSENSUS across the political spectrum — not merely a Nazi demand; (b) FOUNDED ON NATIONALISM AND RACISM; (c) ANTI-COMMUNIST; (d) AND MOST IMPORTANTLY, ANTI-WESTERN IN A PRECISE LEGAL SENSE: IT REJECTS THE EQUAL SOVEREIGNTY OF STATES AS A LEGAL FOUNDATION. That says more than it seems: whoever rejects the equality of sovereigns rejects the very structure of modern international law and replaces it with a hierarchy of nations and greater spaces.

cards.q: Which five currents did interwar theory of international law have?
cards.a: 1) THE VIENNA SCHOOL (KELSEN, KUNZ, VERDROSS). 2) NATURAL-LAW APPROACHES. 3) THE POSITIVISTS. 4) SOVIET INTERNATIONAL LAW. 5) FASCIST INTERNATIONAL LAW.

cards.q: What features did fascist international law have?
cards.a: a) THE FIGHT AGAINST VERSAILLES — in Germany a CONSENSUS across the spectrum, not merely a Nazi demand. b) FOUNDED ON NATIONALISM AND RACISM. c) ANTI-COMMUNIST. d) And above all ANTI-WESTERN IN A PRECISE LEGAL SENSE: IT REJECTS THE EQUAL SOVEREIGNTY OF STATES AS A LEGAL FOUNDATION — whoever rejects the equality of sovereigns rejects the structure of modern international law and replaces it with a HIERARCHY OF NATIONS AND GREATER SPACES.

slides.title: The Hitler–Stalin Pact (23 August 1939)
slides.text: THE 'MOLOTOV-RIBBENTROP PACT' — and Vec adds a literary comparison that is easy to remember: IT WAS THE MODEL FOR ORWELL'S NOVEL 1984. (Two totalitarian powers that turn overnight from enemies into allies and back, without anyone being permitted to mention it.) THE CONTENT: EAST CENTRAL EUROPE WAS DIVIDED INTO SPHERES OF INTEREST — this was in the secret additional protocol, whose existence the USSR denied until 1989. THE CONSEQUENCES: IT ENABLED GERMANY'S ATTACK ON POLAND ON 1 SEPTEMBER 1939; THE USSR CONQUERED THE EASTERN PART OF POLAND AND THE BALTIC STATES. And one irony of international law Vec does not forget: THE USSR WAS EXPELLED FROM THE LEAGUE OF NATIONS IN 1939 — BUT FOR THE ATTACK ON FINLAND, not for the partition of Poland. It is the only expulsion in the League's history, and it came at a moment when the organization was already effectively defunct.

cards.q: What did the Hitler–Stalin Pact contain and what were its consequences?
cards.a: The 'MOLOTOV-RIBBENTROP PACT' of 23 August 1939, the model for ORWELL'S NOVEL 1984. EAST CENTRAL EUROPE WAS DIVIDED INTO SPHERES OF INTEREST (a secret additional protocol whose existence the USSR denied until 1989). It enabled GERMANY'S ATTACK ON POLAND ON 1 SEPTEMBER 1939; the USSR conquered EASTERN POLAND AND THE BALTIC STATES.

cards.q: For what was the USSR expelled from the League of Nations and why is that ironic?
cards.a: IN 1939 FOR THE ATTACK ON FINLAND — NOT for the partition of Poland. It is THE ONLY EXPULSION IN THE LEAGUE'S HISTORY and it came at a moment when the organization was already effectively defunct.

slides.title: Nuremberg and Tokyo: three heads of charge
slides.text: THE INTERNATIONAL MILITARY TRIBUNAL (IMT) WAS CREATED BY A TREATY OF THE FOUR POWERS OCCUPYING GERMANY (the London Agreement, 8 August 1945); its counterpart for the Far East is the IMTFE IN TOKYO. THREE GROUPS OF CHARGES, to be known in this order: (1) WAR CRIMES, (2) CRIMES AGAINST HUMANITY, (3) CRIMES AGAINST PEACE. The last is the most contested, because it was precisely there that it was objected that it punished conduct that had not been punishable when committed. THE SIGNIFICANCE: Vec quotes KLAUS KRESS, for whom Nuremberg and Tokyo are 'THE FIRST PRECEDENT OF INTERNATIONALIZED CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS', and adds that they RECOGNIZED THE EXISTENCE OF INTERNATIONAL CRIMINAL LAW. To this a caution useful for a question about legitimacy: BOTH TRIALS WERE DRIVEN BY DIFFERENT MOTIVES AND DIFFERENT LEGAL CULTURES — it was not a single unified project. And the confirmation: THE UN GENERAL ASSEMBLY AFFIRMED THE NUREMBERG PRINCIPLES IN 1946. BESIDES THE INTERNATIONAL TRIBUNALS, DOMESTIC COURTS ALSO TRIED CASES, and Vec names a series particularly relevant for Austria: THE PEOPLE'S COURTS (VOLKSGERICHTE) IN AUSTRIA, 'EICHMANN IN JERUSALEM', THE AUSCHWITZ TRIAL IN FRANKFURT and THE MURER CASE IN GRAZ.

cards.q: Which three groups of charges did the Nuremberg tribunal have, and which was the most contested?
cards.a: 1) WAR CRIMES. 2) CRIMES AGAINST HUMANITY. 3) CRIMES AGAINST PEACE. The LAST is the most contested, because it was objected that it PUNISHED CONDUCT THAT HAD NOT BEEN PUNISHABLE WHEN COMMITTED. The tribunal was created by A TREATY OF THE FOUR POWERS OCCUPYING GERMANY.

cards.q: Which domestic trials does Vec name besides the international tribunals?
cards.a: THE PEOPLE'S COURTS (VOLKSGERICHTE) IN AUSTRIA, 'EICHMANN IN JERUSALEM', THE AUSCHWITZ TRIAL IN FRANKFURT and THE MURER CASE IN GRAZ. And a caution on legitimacy: BOTH INTERNATIONAL TRIALS WERE DRIVEN BY DIFFERENT MOTIVES AND DIFFERENT LEGAL CULTURES — not a single unified project. The UN General Assembly affirmed the Nuremberg principles IN 1946.

slides.title: The Cold War and decolonization in international law
slides.text: THE COLD WAR is defined as a BIPOLAR CONFRONTATION BETWEEN CAPITALISM AND SOCIALISM WITH OPPOSING CONCEPTIONS OF MODERNITY, which ENDED THE POST-WAR OPTIMISM. And Vec gives an unusual dating worth mentioning: IT BEGINS AS EARLY AS THE 1890s and CULMINATES BETWEEN 1945 AND 1989. That is: not in 1947 but as a long clash of two universalist projects. THE USA AND THE USSR ARE 'TWO POWERFUL EMPIRES WITH AN INTERNATIONAL MISSION', and it is an INTERNATIONAL SYSTEM, because ALL THE LEADING POWERS ALIGN THEIR FOREIGN POLICY BY IT. DECOLONIZATION has three consequences: (1) IT BROUGHT AN INCREASE IN THE NUMBER AND DIVERSITY OF SOVEREIGN STATES; (2) THOSE STATES RAISED THEIR VOICE AND DEVELOPED THEIR OWN LEGAL AND POLITICAL IDEAS AND CLAIMS — so the change was not merely numerical but substantive; (3) AND A SECOND WAVE CAME WITH THE COLLAPSE OF THE SOVIET UNION AT THE END OF THE COLD WAR, WHEN NEW STATES AGAIN CAME INTO BEING. To this Vec names the fields in which treaties were being made at the time, which show well how the subject matter of international law was expanding: DIPLOMATIC RELATIONS (1961), NUCLEAR WEAPONS (1963, 1970 and others), ANTARCTICA (1959) and OUTER SPACE (1967).

cards.q: How does Vec define and date the Cold War?
cards.a: As a BIPOLAR CONFRONTATION BETWEEN CAPITALISM AND SOCIALISM WITH OPPOSING CONCEPTIONS OF MODERNITY, which ENDED THE POST-WAR OPTIMISM. He dates it unusually: IT BEGINS AS EARLY AS THE 1890s and CULMINATES BETWEEN 1945 AND 1989 — that is, as a LONG CLASH OF TWO UNIVERSALIST PROJECTS, not an event of 1947.

cards.q: Which three consequences did decolonization have for international law, and in which new fields were treaties made?
cards.a: 1) AN INCREASE IN THE NUMBER AND DIVERSITY OF SOVEREIGN STATES. 2) Those states RAISED THEIR VOICE AND DEVELOPED THEIR OWN LEGAL AND POLITICAL IDEAS — the change was not merely numerical but substantive. 3) A SECOND WAVE with the COLLAPSE OF THE USSR. New treaty fields: DIPLOMATIC RELATIONS (1961), NUCLEAR WEAPONS (1963, 1970), ANTARCTICA (1959), OUTER SPACE (1967).

slides.title: International criminal law: decades without progress
slides.text: Vec sums up the post-war fate of international criminal law in three sentences that belong together and are best known as a whole. (1) NO PROGRESS FOR DECADES. (2) THE REASON: HUMAN RIGHTS WERE A BATTLEGROUND BETWEEN THE POLITICAL BLOCS — each side measured the other by them, so nothing could be agreed that might rebound on itself. (3) THE BREAKTHROUGH CAME ONLY WITH THE AD HOC TRIBUNALS: THE ICTY ESTABLISHED IN 1993, OPERATIONAL IN 1994; THE ICTR ESTABLISHED IN 1994, OPERATIONAL IN 1997. And the conclusion, which links directly to Kress in the required reading: THE ICTY AND THE ICTR CLEARED THE WAY FOR THE SECOND GENERATION OF INTERNATIONAL CRIMINAL LAW. THE 21ST-CENTURY DISPUTES Vec names as open: 'HUMANITARIAN INTERVENTION' AND ITS LEGALITY and 'NEW WARS'; TOO MANY SUBSYSTEMS, that is, the question of THE FRAGMENTATION OF INTERNATIONAL LAW; TWAIL AND FEMINIST CRITIQUE (TWAIL = Third World Approaches to International Law); and UNIVERSAL JURISDICTION.

terms.def: Third World Approaches to International Law — Third World critical approaches to international law.

cards.q: Why was there no progress in international criminal law for decades after 1945?
cards.a: Because HUMAN RIGHTS WERE A BATTLEGROUND BETWEEN THE POLITICAL BLOCS — each side measured the other by them, so nothing could be agreed that might rebound on itself. The breakthrough came only with the AD HOC TRIBUNALS: the ICTY established 1993 (operational 1994), the ICTR established 1994 (operational 1997) — and they CLEARED THE WAY FOR THE SECOND GENERATION of international criminal law.

cards.q: Which 20th- and 21st-century disputes remain open in international law?
cards.a: 'HUMANITARIAN INTERVENTION' AND ITS LEGALITY and 'NEW WARS'; TOO MANY SUBSYSTEMS, that is, THE FRAGMENTATION OF INTERNATIONAL LAW; TWAIL (Third World Approaches to International Law) AND FEMINIST CRITIQUE; and UNIVERSAL JURISDICTION.
